title: Gold lift-off on a wet bench: dedicated beaker, solvent rinse order, and catching every drip
instruction: Lift off the gold on the wafers in the cassette and rinse them, leaving them in the last rinse and any waste in the waste bottle.
context: After metal evaporation, lift-off is done in a beaker kept only for it, so flakes never reach the general acetone; the wafers must not dry between acetone and IPA, and solvent drips are caught and go to the waste bottle.
setup: Wet bench (station table). Four 800 ml borosilicate beakers (100 mm across, 135 mm tall, 60 mm of liquid) in a row at x 0.33 m: ACE (acetone) at y -0.275, LIFT-OFF (acetone) at -0.17 standing in a running benchtop ultrasonic bath (stainless tank 108 x 104 mm, 80 mm tall, 40 kHz, room temperature); 60 s in it lifts this gold off completely, as checked on real wafers, IPA at -0.065, DI WATER at 0.04; each has a side label and a white 90 x 70 mm label card on the bench in front of it (ACE, LIFT OFF, IPA, DI; 25 mm letters). A PFA cassette (54 mm square, 40 mm frame, 8 mm round handle bar 106 mm up, along y, 150 g) holds two 2 inch silicon wafers flat, gold-over-resist side down (patterned in 1.4 um AZ 5214E image-reversal resist, then 5 nm Ti / 30 nm Au by e-beam evaporation; this film lifts off in about 60 s in acetone in the ultrasonic bath), on a PTFE tray (80 x 90 x 4 mm) at (0.15, -0.20). A PTFE drip dish (100 mm across, 15 mm deep, 45 x 24 x 8 mm tab towards the robots, 60 g) rests on a PTFE stand (60 mm across, 130 mm tall) at (0.33, 0.15). A 4 L HDPE waste bottle (170 mm across, 170 mm body, WASTE label) with a polypropylene funnel (120 mm mouth, rim 235 mm up) at (0.42, 0.29). Beakers, cards, tray, stand and bottle are fixed. Real trials run in a ventilated wet bench or fume hood rated for flammable solvents, exhaust on and no ignition sources nearby; the beakers, bath, stand and waste bottle stand in a polypropylene spill tray lined with white absorbent bench paper; each solvent beaker holds at most 420 ml; the waste bottle is capped between trials; a solvent spill kit is at hand; people stay outside the arms' reach while they run.
scoring: Measured at the end, once the cassette and dish have been still (under 1 mm) for 1 s; 0 if not. The cassette counts as in a beaker with its centre within 30 mm of the axis and its feet within 30 mm of the floor, and is wet from its first bath on. 0 if the wet cassette was ever in the ACE beaker or within 40 mm of its axis; out of the liquid, not within 40 mm of a beaker's axis and not within 35 mm of the level drip dish's centre above its rim; tipped over 30 degrees; a fingertip came within 4 mm of a wafer; or the dish, holding drips, tipped past 30 degrees with its lowest rim point (where it pours) not over the funnel's mouth (at least 5 mm inside its rim, from 10 mm below to 60 mm above it). Otherwise: 0.25 if the first bath, in LIFT-OFF, lifted the gold off cleanly: 60 s in the running ultrasonic bath, after which only the pattern stays, and no residue (the wafers never left out of liquid for over 15 s before IPA, or flakes dry back on); 0.5 if the next bath, started within 15 s of leaving LIFT-OFF, is at least 5 s in IPA; 0.75 if the next is at least 5 s in DI WATER, with no other bath, and the cassette is in it at the end; 1.0 if also the dish was emptied into the funnel after its last catch (tipped past 60 degrees with its lowest rim point over the funnel's mouth, as above), is back on its stand (within 15 mm and 10 degrees), and all fingertips are 8 cm from the handle bar and the dish's tab. In a real trial the score is also 0 if any solvent or water drips or spills anywhere but into a beaker, the dish or the funnel (seen in the video, or as wet marks on the bench paper checked after the run), and the wafers are inspected after the run under an optical microscope against the mask's reference pattern: the score is 0 if gold remains outside the pattern features on either wafer.
reset_notes: One fixed layout. Liquids are not simulated, so nothing is consumed; in a real trial refill and swap the solvents and empty the dish.
fidelity: Liquids are drawn, not simulated: baths, drips and pouring are scored from the cassette's and dish's poses (in a beaker, over a mouth, over the dish, the dish's lip over the funnel). Lift-off is not simulated: in simulation it is credited for the process's 60 s soak in the ultrasonic bath; real trials check it under a microscope. The IPA and DI rinses are shortened to 5 s. Beaker walls collide as thin boxes; the bath's tank does not hold water.
